title: AP-MT063-AcpClientServices

scope.summary:
GOAL: Implement the CLIENT-side services of ACP — the JSON-RPC methods the AGENT calls back INTO Handshake during a turn. Under ACP the client (Handshake) is the agent's execution environment: permission arbitration, filesystem access, and terminal execution are all client-implemented services. This MT delivers: (1) session/request_permission routed through the Handshake ConsentGate with DENY-BY-DEFAULT on timeout; (2) fs/read_text_file plus the fs write counterpart (fs/write_text_file) scoped STRICTLY to the session worktree; (3) terminal/create (and its companion terminal methods when the capability is advertised) routed through the sandbox adapter policy; (4) EVERY service call ledgered as a typed event — the agent's actions inside Handshake must be fully attributable and reconstructable.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New file src/backend/handshake_core/src/agent_sessions/acp/client_services.rs (service handler implementations + worktree scope guard + capability advertisement wiring) plus small wiring lines in acp/mod.rs and acp/client_core.rs (register handlers on the crate's client connection; advertise fs/terminal capabilities in initialize). Integration tests in src/backend/handshake_core/tests/acp_client_services.rs against the MT-061 fixture agent extended to issue scripted service calls.

DETAILED SPEC:
- PERMISSIONS (session/request_permission): the agent sends a permission request with a set of options (allow/reject variants, once/always kinds per the ACP schema). Route the request to the Handshake ConsentGate (src/backend/handshake_core/src/model_runtime/cloud/consent_gate.rs — reuse via its public API, do not fork). Mapping rules: a ConsentGate approval selects the agent-offered allow option (prefer the once-scoped option unless the gate verdict is an always-scope grant); a denial selects the reject option; a TIMEOUT or unavailable gate DENIES (deny-by-default, selecting the reject option) — never auto-allow. If the turn was cancelled while the permission request was pending, respond with the ACP cancelled outcome for the request. Every request/verdict pair is ledgered with option ids and latency.
- FILESYSTEM (fs/read_text_file, fs/write_text_file): only when the session capability was advertised. Path scope guard: canonicalize the requested path and require it to be inside the session worktree root (the MT-001 session model binding) — reject absolute paths outside the root, .. traversal, symlink/junction escapes (canonicalize BEFORE the prefix check), and non-worktree drives. Windows specifics are first-class: case-insensitive comparison, drive-letter normalization, verbatim (\\?\) prefix tolerance, and paths containing spaces (the operator's real worktree roots contain spaces). Honor the ACP line/limit read parameters; writes create parent directories only inside the scope. Out-of-scope requests return a typed JSON-RPC error to the agent AND a ledgered scope-violation event — the turn continues (the agent is told no; Handshake does not crash the session).
- TERMINAL (terminal/create + terminal/output, terminal/wait_for_exit, terminal/kill, terminal/release): advertised ONLY when the sandbox adapter policy for the session permits terminal execution. terminal/create routes through the sandbox adapter layer (src/backend/handshake_core/src/sandbox/ — adapter.rs trait + registry.rs/selection.rs choose the concrete adapter; reuse via API, do not fork) with cwd pinned inside the session worktree and the process registered with ownership metadata per HBR-QUIET-003 (owner_session, owner_wp, owner_role, started_at) and reclaimed at session close. Hidden window, no focus steal (HBR-QUIET-001/002). terminal/kill maps to supervised termination; terminal/release detaches per ACP semantics but ownership/reclamation remains with the session.
- CAPABILITY ADVERTISEMENT: initialize (MT-061) must advertise exactly what this MT implements: fs.readTextFile=true, fs.writeTextFile=true, terminal=true only when sandbox policy allows for the session; never advertise a service that would fail.
- LEDGER: every service call (method, params digest, verdict/result class, duration, session id, turn id) emits a typed EventLedger event; a TraceProjection over the ledger answers 'what did the agent touch and who allowed it' with zero chat history (HBR-INT-007).

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read the agent-client-protocol crate's Client trait surface for the service handler signatures, the ConsentGate public API, and the sandbox adapter.rs/registry.rs/selection.rs API before writing code.
2. Implement the worktree scope guard as a small pure function (canonicalize + normalized prefix check) with exhaustive Windows unit tests (traversal, symlink escape, case, drive letter, verbatim prefix, spaces).
3. Implement fs/read_text_file (line/limit honored) and fs/write_text_file behind the scope guard; typed errors for out-of-scope.
4. Implement session/request_permission -> ConsentGate routing with the option-mapping rules and the deny-by-default timeout arm (tokio timeout around the gate future; timeout duration configurable with a conservative default).
5. Implement terminal/create + companions through the sandbox adapter policy with HBR-QUIET-003 ownership registration and session-close reclamation.
6. Wire capability advertisement in initialize to reflect the implemented services and the per-session sandbox policy verdict.
7. Emit typed EventLedger events for every service call; wire HBR-INT-009 tier evidence.
8. Extend the fixture agent with scripted service-call sequences: permission (each outcome), in-scope and out-of-scope fs reads/writes, terminal create/wait/kill.
9. Author the integration tests listed in expected_tests and run the proof targets.
forbidden_paths: .GOV/** (the bridge is READ-ONLY reference for parity; never edited by this WP)
src/frontend/** (no GUI surface in this MT)
acceptance_criteria: session/request_permission routes to ConsentGate: approval selects the agent-offered allow option, denial selects reject, and a gate TIMEOUT selects reject (deny-by-default) — all three proven by tests with the fixture agent asserting which option id it received.
A permission request pending when the turn is cancelled resolves with the ACP cancelled outcome — proven by test.
fs/read_text_file returns worktree file content honoring line/limit parameters; fs/write_text_file writes inside the worktree — proven by tests.

The scope guard rejects: absolute path outside the worktree, .. traversal, symlink/junction escape (canonicalized before check), other-drive paths — each rejection is a typed JSON-RPC error to the agent plus a ledgered scope-violation event, and the session survives — proven by parameterized tests.
Windows path handling proven: case-insensitive match, drive-letter normalization, verbatim prefix tolerance, and a worktree root containing spaces — unit tests on the scope guard.

terminal/create only succeeds when sandbox policy allows; the spawned process carries HBR-QUIET-003 ownership metadata and is reclaimed at session close (no leaked pid) — proven by test; when policy forbids, the terminal capability is NOT advertised at initialize and a direct call returns a typed error.
Capability advertisement matches implementation exactly (fs true/true; terminal reflects policy) — proven by initialize negotiation test.
Every service call emits a typed EventLedger event (method, result class, duration, session/turn ids); a test reconstructs the agent's full service-call history from the ledger alone.
cargo build -p handshake_core green; all listed tests pass headless with zero visible windows (HBR-QUIET-001/002).
expected_tests: acp_fs_scope_guard_windows_normalization (case, drive letter, verbatim prefix, spaces in root)
implementation_notes: ConsentGate already exists at src/backend/handshake_core/src/model_runtime/cloud/consent_gate.rs (WP-1 lineage) — this MT consumes its public API. If its API cannot express a bounded-timeout arbitration, record a typed dependency blocker per HBR-STOP-004 rather than forking a second consent surface.

Deny-by-default is the WP-017 stub red-team stance (consent gates always enforced): a permission timeout, a crashed gate, or an unroutable request all resolve to the agent's reject option. There is no allow fallback anywhere in this MT.

The scope guard canonicalizes BEFORE prefix-checking; on Windows use std::fs::canonicalize semantics (returns verbatim paths) and normalize both sides identically. The operator's real roots look like 'D:/Projects/LLM projects/Handshake/Handshake Worktrees/<wt>' — spaces are the norm, not the edge case.

The governed-broker precedent (.GOV/tools/handshake-acp-bridge/agent.mjs) validates worktree identity/drift before every request (validateGovernedRequest: local_worktree_dir drift, worktree existence) — the product analogue is the MT-001 session worktree binding this MT scopes against; parity is measured in MT-065.

terminal/release semantics: ACP lets the agent release a terminal it no longer waits on; Handshake ownership does NOT transfer — the session still owns and reclaims the process at close (HBR-QUIET-003).

fs write counterpart method name: the ACP schema names it fs/write_text_file; verify the exact method constant against the pinned agent-client-protocol crate version at implementation time and follow the crate, not this prose, if they differ (record the correction in lifecycle).

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Headless backend MT: client services are agent-facing JSON-RPC handlers; the operator-facing consent UI is the existing ConsentGate surface (reused, not created here). Proof via ledger/TraceProjection per HBR-VIS-004.

target_entries: Agent sessions: what an ACP agent may touch — worktree-scoped filesystem, consent-gated permissions (deny-by-default on timeout), sandbox-policied terminals

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations: FLIGHT_RECORDER: permission verdicts, scope violations, and terminal lifecycle are business events — FR emit per MT-161 kinds when landed, else DEFERRED-with-reason.
INTERNAL_DIAGNOSTICS: expose pending-permission count/age and live agent-terminal count to the open diagnostic-event API — WIRED or DEFERRED-with-reason.
PALMISTRY: agent-created terminal processes are freeze/leak candidates that outlive UI health — register them with the external watcher's process tracking, or DEFERRED-with-reason.
risk_if_missed: ACP agents cannot request permissions, read/write files, or run commands through Handshake — real agents (claude-agent-acp) stall on their first service call, MT-065's end-to-end repo-gov workflow is impossible, and any interim workaround would hand agents unscoped host access.

risks: RISK-1: Sandbox escape via fs services — a traversal/symlink/junction or Windows-normalization gap in the scope guard hands the agent arbitrary host filesystem access under Handshake's identity.
RISK-2: Permission auto-allow — a timeout/crash path that resolves to allow (or that answers before the operator) silently converts the ConsentGate into a rubber stamp.

RISK-3: Orphaned agent terminals — terminal/create processes without ownership metadata or close-time reclamation accumulate as unattributable background processes (the exact class HBR-QUIET-003 and the bridge's terminal-reclaim duty exist to prevent).

RISK-4: Capability lie — advertising terminal or fs capabilities that the policy then rejects makes conforming agents fail mid-turn in confusing ways; the inverse (silent extra services) widens the attack surface unannounced.
RISK-5: Unattributed agent actions — service calls that bypass the ledger leave no answer to 'what did the agent do', breaking the WP-017 injection/attribution stance.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): canonicalize-then-prefix-check scope guard as a pure function with parameterized escape tests including Windows-specific cases; out-of-scope is a typed error, never a fallback path.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): deny-by-default is structural — the timeout arm and every error arm select the reject option; a dedicated test kills the gate future and asserts rejection.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): HBR-QUIET-003 ownership metadata on every terminal spawn + session-close reclamation test asserting zero surviving pids.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): capability advertisement is derived from the same policy objects that gate the handlers (single source); negotiation test asserts advertisement==enforcement.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): ledger emit is inside each handler's single exit path; reconstruction test proves completeness against the fixture agent's scripted call list.

research_provenance.source: agentclientprotocol.com (client-implemented services: session/request_permission with option selection incl. cancelled outcome, fs/read_text_file with line/limit, fs/write_text_file, terminal/create + output/wait_for_exit/kill/release, capability advertisement at initialize) + inspected product code: model_runtime/cloud/consent_gate.rs (existing consent surface), sandbox/adapter.rs + registry.rs + selection.rs (adapter policy layer) + .GOV/tools/handshake-acp-bridge/agent.mjs (worktree identity validation + terminal reclamation duties as parity reference).
corrections: Deny-by-default on permission timeout is stricter than the ACP spec requires (spec leaves arbitration to the client) — Handshake policy per the WP-017 stub red-team controls.
Terminal capability is per-session policy-derived, not global: sandbox adapter selection decides, and advertisement must match enforcement.
Exact fs write method constant to be verified against the pinned crate version at implementation time; crate wins over contract prose with a recorded correction.
